decisions.executionNote: Raise and pitch the right gripper above the mouse; left arm stays clear. Mouse is closer to the robot than in the reference.
Continue pitching downward and align the open fingers over the mouse. Slow descent preserves elbow-up continuity.
Lower a little, close around the mouse, and make a short test lift. Retention will be checked visually.
Mouse retention is uncertain; reopen and approach lower and slightly farther back for a deeper side grasp.
Lift the mouse with closed fingers and begin transfer toward the pad, checking that it follows the gripper.
Mouse visibly follows the right gripper. Move above the center of its pad and start lowering while maintaining the grasp.
Set the mouse down on the pad, open the gripper, and lift clear to verify placement.
Mouse rests on the pad. Reposition both arms toward separate left and right contact points along the keyboard's front edge.
Bring closed fingertips to two spaced front-edge pushing positions, with each arm remaining on its own side.
Lower the closed tips to the keyboard edge and establish a gentle, balanced forward push; verify keyboard motion before continuing.
Keyboard moved forward. Continue toward the frame with a small rightward bias and slightly more right-side advance to straighten it.
Gently finish the keyboard's forward alignment with the frame, keeping the left hand left of center and correcting the small skew.
Keyboard is aligned over the frame. Open and lift both hands clear; bring the left arm toward the figurine while the right retracts.
Approach the figurine from above and in front with the left gripper open. Return the right arm toward its original clear position.
Lower around the figurine's upper body, close the left fingers, and test a small lift. The base must follow before transfer.
Lift the figurine clear and begin moving toward the small stand, keeping the left grasp closed and checking base retention.
The figurine stayed on the table, so the grasp failed. Reopen and approach lower around its torso rather than its head.
Center the fingers slightly left and lower around the figurine's torso, close fully, and test a vertical lift before translating.
Fingers appear to have closed in front of the torso. Reopen and advance deeper around the body, then make another short lift.
Test whether the deeper shoulder grasp retains the figurine by lifting vertically, then making a small motion toward the stand.
The figurine and its base now lift together. Carry it toward the small stand with the left grasp closed and a clear height.
Align the hanging figurine's base over the stand and lower gradually. The grasp remains closed until the base is supported.
Figurine slipped near the stand and is not upright. Release and clear it, then approach the displaced alarm clock; figurine orientation may need correction.
Align the open left fingers with the alarm clock's sides and descend from above. Keep the right hand parked clear.
Center and deepen the clock grasp, close the left fingers, then make a short vertical retention test.
The clock is between the fingers. Lift it above the drawer's rim before carrying it left and back onto the top surface.
Clock retention is visible. Continue lifting and translating toward the drawer top without changing the grasp orientation.
Continuity guard stopped the previous approach. Replan from the observed pose with smaller movements and a gradual shallower wrist pitch while retaining the clock.
Avoid further upward motion near the elbow continuity limit. Shift left toward the drawer center and gradually level the held clock before advancing.
The lateral adjustment improved elbow clearance. Advance slowly over the drawer rim with a small lift and shallower pitch, keeping the clock retained.
The guard again stopped forward/upward motion. Keep the flange back, lower it slightly, and pivot the clock upward over the rim without forcing the elbow.
Clock is above the drawer top with improved elbow clearance. Lower it gently onto the surface, open the fingers, and begin withdrawing.
Clock rests on the drawer. Withdraw clear and orient the left gripper downward to recover the fallen figurine near its stand.
Center the open left gripper over the fallen figurine's torso and descend for a top-down grasp, staying clear of the keyboard.
Deepen and center the grasp on the fallen figurine's chest, close the fingers, and make a small vertical retention test.
The first top-down grasp was too high. Reopen, descend around the torso sides, close, and test again with a short lift.
Move the open fingers farther along the torso, away from the narrow neck, then close and test retention again.
The figurine still appears table-supported. Reopen and lower the fingers substantially around its torso sides, then close and test a short lift.
The deeper grasp appears to hold the figurine's torso. Lift it clear of the table before attempting to restore its upright orientation.
The figurine slipped during the lift. Recenter leftward over the chest and approach deeper between the body and arms, rather than gripping an outer limb.
The open fingers displaced the figurine and are over its legs. Lift clear, move toward the visible chest nearer the robot, and reapproach without dragging.
Make a small chest-centering adjustment, close around the body rather than its head, and lift vertically to check retention.
The chest was still below the pinch region. Reopen, lower around the torso with a small forward correction, then close and test a short lift.
The deeper torso grasp now visibly encloses the figurine. Lift clear, then start rotating its head upward and base downward while keeping the grasp closed.
Figurine remains in the grasp above the table. Continue rotating it upright while moving gradually toward the stand, with the base kept clear.
The figurine is now upright in the grasp. Replan after the guard: use a small lateral shift and yaw to improve elbow clearance while moving toward its stand.
Set the recovered figurine upright on the table and release before the elbow limit. Retreat to obtain a safer front approach for moving it onto the stand.
The figurine stands on its base. Reorient and retract the open left gripper to approach its torso from the front with a less folded elbow.
Square the left gripper to the upright torso, center it slightly left, and close for a forward-facing transfer to the stand.
Test the centered torso grasp with a small lift, then advance toward the stand without rotating the figurine or approaching the elbow limit.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Carry the upright figurine toward the stand at constant height, keeping the right arm stationary.
Align the figurine base over the small stand, lower gently, then open the fingers while holding the wrist still to avoid toppling it.
The figurine stands over its stand with fingers open. Withdraw without contact and begin returning both arms to their original clear poses.
All four main items appear placed and the figurine remains standing. Continue the left arm's unobstructed return toward its initial pose.
Complete the small remaining return-to-origin motion with both grippers open, preserving the placed objects.
Both arms reached origin and the four main items remain placed. Begin the remaining drawer task by approaching its handle with the left gripper open.
Turn the left jaws vertical to pinch the horizontal drawer handle, and advance slowly while adjusting alignment from the wrist view.
Use the rolled wrist view to center the open vertical jaws on the handle, moving slightly lower and left while advancing cautiously.
Advance just enough to enclose the handle, close the vertical jaws, and test a short straight pull while watching for drawer motion.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Reach deeper with open fingers, close on the handle, and test the drawer pull with the right arm stationary.
The handle has not followed either pull. Keep the jaws open and inspect a deeper approach before closing again; stop short of forcing the drawer face.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Close at the deeper handle position, then gently pull straight back with the right arm stationary.
The drawer still has not followed the gripper. Adjust the pinch upward to the handle's center, close, and test another short straight pull.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Reopen and lower to center the handle in the vertical jaws, then close and test a short straight pull.
The handle is now visibly between the jaws. Pull straight toward the robot with the grasp closed, checking for drawer translation.
The handle did not follow the pull. Reopen and approach farther so the finger pads, not just their tips, surround the handle at its height.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Back off from the face, center leftward on the handle, close, and test a short pull with the right arm stationary.
The handle appears enclosed. Continue a slow straight pull and check whether the drawer follows rather than inferring success from finger closure.
The drawer did not move with the pull. Release and withdraw rather than forcing it, preserving the four placed items and returning toward the origin.
